## Motivation: Does AI Green the Economy?

**The promise:**
AI and digital technologies → efficiency gains → lower energy per unit of output → reduced ecological footprint

**The paradox (Jevons 1865):**
> "The economical use of fuel is not equivalent to a diminished consumption. The very contrary is the truth."

**The AI energy fact:**
- Each AI query: ~10× energy of a Google search *(Goldman Sachs 2024)*
- Global data centre electricity: set to double by 2026 *(IEA 2024)*
- NVIDIA GPU demand surging while renewables lag

**Research question:** Does ICT/AI adoption reduce ecological footprint in OECD economies — or does the Jevons rebound dominate?

---

## Theory: Environmental Kuznets Curve × Jevons

**EKC hypothesis:** Pollution rises with income, then falls beyond a threshold

**AI-Jevons extension:**

$$EF_{it} = \alpha + \theta_1 \cdot ICT_{it} + \theta_2 \cdot ICT_{it}^2 + \gamma \cdot \mathbf{X}_{it} + \mu_i + \varepsilon_{it}$$

- $\theta_1 > 0, \theta_2 < 0$: Inverted-U in ICT adoption (Jevons rebound then efficiency)
- Turning point: $ICT^* = -\theta_1 / (2\theta_2)$

**Income threshold hypothesis:**

$$EF_{it} = \alpha + \beta_1 \cdot ICT_{it} + \beta_2 \cdot \ln GDP_{it} + \beta_3 \cdot (ICT \times \ln GDP)_{it} + \varepsilon_{it}$$

- $\beta_3 < 0$: Green ICT effect stronger at higher income levels

---

## Data

**Panel:** N = 30 OECD economies, T = 2010–2022 (balanced)

| Variable | Source | Unit |
|----------|--------|------|
| Ecological footprint | Global Footprint Network | gha per capita |
| ICT adoption | World Bank WDI | Internet users (% pop.) |
| GDP per capita | World Bank WDI | PPP, constant 2015 USD |
| Trade openness | World Bank WDI | % GDP |
| FDI net inflows | World Bank WDI | % GDP |
| Renewable energy share | World Bank WDI | % total final energy |
| Urban population | World Bank WDI | % total |

**Estimation sequence:** CD test → CIPS → Westerlund ECM → DK-FE → EKC → System-GMM → Hausman-Taylor IV → DH causality

---

## Pre-Test Results

| Test | Statistic | Decision |
|------|-----------|----------|
| Pesaran CD — Ecological Footprint | z = 18.37*** | Cross-section dependence ✓ |
| Pesaran CD — ICT | z = 24.15*** | CSD confirmed ✓ |
| CIPS — all variables (levels) | > −2.34 | I(1) |
| CIPS — all variables (differences) | < −2.34 | I(0) ✓ |
| Westerlund ECM (Gt) | −2.11** | Cointegration ✓ |
| P-Y Slope heterogeneity | 156.25*** | Heterogeneous slopes ✓ |

**Implication:** CSD + I(1) + heterogeneous slopes → Driscoll-Kraay FE is the appropriate primary estimator (2nd-generation, robust to CSD and serial correlation)

---

## Main Result 1: Direct ICT Effect

**Driscoll-Kraay Fixed Effects — Baseline:**

$$\hat{\beta}_{ICT} = -0.0604 \quad (SE = 0.033, \; p = 0.068)$$

- Borderline significant at 10% level
- ICT reduces ecological footprint — but the effect is weak
- Suggests efficiency gains are **largely offset by rebound demand**

**With income interaction:**

$$\hat{\beta}_{ICT \times \ln GDP} = -0.2709^{***} \quad (p < 0.001)$$

$$\Rightarrow \text{Income threshold} = \mathbf{\$31{,}725 \text{ GDP per capita (PPP)}}$$

- **Below threshold:** ICT adoption increases footprint (Jevons dominates)
- **Above threshold:** ICT adoption decreases footprint (efficiency wins)
- ~60% of OECD sample is **above** threshold

---

## Main Result 2: AI-EKC Turning Point

**Quadratic ICT Specification:**

| Parameter | Estimate | Significance |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| $\theta_1$ (ICT level) | +0.1046 | ** (p = 0.012) |
| $\theta_2$ (ICT squared) | −0.0551 | *** (p = 0.004) |
| GDP per capita | +0.388 | *** |
| Renewable share | −0.071 | ** |

**→ AI-EKC turning point: ICT penetration = 2.584%**

**Interpretation:**

- Phase 1 (ICT < 2.58%): Rising ICT → rising footprint (Jevons rebound)
- Phase 2 (ICT > 2.58%): Rising ICT → falling footprint (efficiency effect)
- Most OECD economies are in the **transition zone** (1.5%–4.5% ICT intensity)

---

## Robustness: System-GMM

**Blundell-Bond System-GMM (lags 2–3, Windmeijer-corrected SE):**

| Variable | Coefficient | Sig. |
|----------|-------------|------|
| Footprint (t−1) | 0.892 | *** |
| ICT adoption | −0.0018 | n.s. |
| GDP per capita | 0.431 | *** |
| Trade openness | −0.089 | * |

**Specification tests:**

- AR(2) test: p = 0.412 ✓ (no second-order serial correlation)
- Sargan J-test: p = 0.183 ✓ (instruments valid)

**Finding:** ICT effect disappears in dynamic specification → short-run rebound dominates; long-run cointegration path required for green transition

---

## Robustness: Hausman-Taylor IV

**Addressing endogeneity of ICT adoption:**

$$\hat{\beta}_{ICT} \text{ (Hausman-Taylor)} = +0.0852 \quad (p = 0.11, \text{ n.s.})$$

**Sign reversal** from DK (−0.060) to HT (+0.085) reveals **proxy sensitivity:**

- Internet penetration is an imperfect AI proxy
- Richer countries adopt more ICT AND have larger footprints (endogeneity)
- AI-specific data (GPU clusters, data centre shares) needed for clean identification

**Honest reporting:** We document this sensitivity rather than suppressing it — it motivates better AI measurement in macro panels.

---

## Dumitrescu-Hurlin Causality

*⚠ Pre-diagnostic under CSD — reported with caveat (1st-generation test)*

| Direction | W̃-statistic | p-value |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| ICT → Ecological Footprint | 3.87 | *** |
| Ecological Footprint → ICT | 2.94 | *** |

**Bidirectional feedback confirmed:**

- ICT adoption precedes footprint changes (AI → environment)
- Environmental pressure spurs ICT investment (environment → AI)

**Implication:** ICT and ecological outcomes are **dynamically co-evolving** — not a simple unidirectional green solution

*(NK2024 PANIC-VAR causality recommended for CSD-robust inference — future work)*

---

## Results Summary

| Finding | Magnitude | Confidence |
|---------|-----------|-----------|
| Direct ICT effect (DK-FE) | β = −0.060 | 10% (borderline) |
| **Income threshold** | **$31,725 per capita** | *** |
| **AI-EKC turning point** | **ICT = 2.58%** | *** |
| Short-run dynamic (GMM) | n.s. | — |
| Long-run cointegration | Confirmed | ** |
| Causality | Bidirectional | *** |

**The Jevons verdict:** AI reduces ecological footprint **only conditionally** — above income and adoption thresholds. Below these, rebound dominates.

---

## Policy Implications

**1. Threshold-aware AI policy**
Countries below $31,725 GDP/capita should not assume AI auto-greenifies the economy. Direct regulation of data centre energy intensity is needed.

**2. AI-specific energy accounting**
Macro panels need AI compute intensity data (GPU-hours, FLOP/joule), not just internet penetration. Eurostat and OECD should standardise reporting.

**3. Above-threshold OECD leaders**
For Scandinavia, Switzerland, USA: accelerate ICT–renewable energy co-investment. The green payoff is within reach but not guaranteed without clean energy infrastructure.

**4. Rebound management**
Energy efficiency standards for AI hardware (EU AI Act energy annex) can compress the Jevons rebound phase.

---

## Conclusions

**Main findings:**

✓ AI reduces ecological footprint — but **conditionally only**

✓ **Income threshold:** $31,725 per capita — below this, Jevons rebound dominates

✓ **AI-EKC turning point:** 2.58% ICT intensity — inverted-U confirmed

✓ Short-run rebound, long-run cointegration — ICT is a slow green technology

✓ Proxy sensitivity (Hausman-Taylor): better AI-specific data urgently needed

**Policy warning:** Automatic optimism about AI as a green technology is empirically unjustified for lower-income OECD members.
